page.overview:
Who is Mike Hawthorn?

John Michael Hawthorn (10 April 1929 – 22 January 1959) was a racing driver, born in Mexborough, Yorkshire, England, and educated at Ardingly College, West Sussex.

Mike Hawthorn made his competition debut driving his 1934 Riley Ulster Imp, KV 9475, winning the 1,100 c.c. sports car class at the [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brighton_Speed_Trials Brighton Speed Trials] on 2 September 1950.[http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Hawthorn#cite_note-1 [2]] In 1951, driving a 1½-litre T.T. Riley, he entered the Motor Sport Brooklands Memorial Trophy, a season-long contest run at [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodwood_Circuit Goodwood], winning it by one point.[http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Hawthorn#cite_note-2 [3]] He also won the Ulster Trophy Handicap at [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dundrod_Circuit Dundrod] and the Leinster Trophy at Wicklow that year.[http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Hawthorn#cite_note-3 [4]]

Hawthorn made his Formula One debut at the 1952 Belgian Grand Prix, finishing in fourth place. He won his first Grand Prix, at the ninth attempt, at the 1953 French Grand Prix at Reims.

After winning the title, Hawthorn immediately announced his retirement from Formula One, having been badly affected by the death of his close friend and Ferrari teammate Peter Collins in that year's German Grand Prix.
